chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Bebop-minded players in his Dallas band
summary: Smith says young players in his band thought themselves bebop but lacked substance, though a few such as Curtis White were good.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: [AT 2 MINUTES] In a band like this, were the musicians passing through reflecting the new changes in music?
Did most of the guys in the band really think of themselves as bebop players?
Yeah. We had two or three of them in there. We had a trumpet player I was telling you about a while ago in that band, and a tenor player. Yeah, they was goin' wild!

No, no. No, they didn't have no meat in 'em. They could read, good readers, but playing solo they seemed stuck right on the (?) and right in the middle of the choruses. It didn't make no difference to them. But the second time, I'd just
You didn't have any good ones? You didn't have any really great players?
Yeah, I had two or three of them that came through here and that stayed with a while.
A boy named Curtis White. He was good.
He played trumpet. And then I had a tenor player, I can't think of... And Milton Thomas. Chester Thomas. They two brothers; they was good. Yeah, they're here now, living right down on (?) .
